### 05 · FLOW INTO THE CURRENT (interactive): pilot screen, detailed

`references/05_flow_into_the_current.png` vs `screenshots/05.png` (`qa/05_side_by_side.png`). Live state at capture:
stage 05, s=144.18, coins 1,420, hearts 5, cam (4.75, −37.93, −79.82). Live rig at `81e639e` (`STAGE_CAM['05']`):
back 6.4, up 4.1, ahead 18, lookUp 1.8, vFOV 62, latFollow 0.6, roll 0.5.

Verdict: the HUD values and the general ingredients are right. The geometry reads as a bending spring of orange pipes in a blue-lilac tube, where the reference is a **straight** magenta tube with concentric gold bands and a meandering water floor. Benny sits too low and is seen too steeply.

#### 5.1 Camera, height and vanishing point

| | Reference | Live |
|---|---|---|
| VP | **(498, 479) = 57.6% x / 31.2% y** (measured). Every ring is concentric about it. | Brightest point (471, 478) lies in a white glare band (y≈500–700). Rings are **not** concentric, so there is no single VP. |
| Pitch | Implied at vFOV 62°: view axis ≈12.7° below the tube axis, ≈3° left of it | Stream and coin line **climb** toward the upper centre; the view looks up a rising, bending tube |
| Camera height over Benny | Low elevation (estimated 10–20°): the hat brim is a shallow ellipse and the whole back of the body is visible | Steep (≈25–30° from the rig numbers): the hat crown fills the view and the body is hidden |
| Benny in frame | x 230–612, y 768–1190: height 27%, centre 49%, **bottom 77%** | x 265–605, y 1062–1450: height 25%, centre 51%, **bottom 94%**. About 290 px (19% of frame) too low |
| Benny vs VP | Benny's centre is 32.5% of frame height below the VP | 50.8% below |

#### 5.2 Tube straightness
* **Reference**: the visible tube stretch is **straight**; ≈10 rings sit concentric around one point. All the S-curves are in the
  **water bands on the floor**. The tube itself does not bend.
* **Live**: the tube bends inside the visible range, so successive rings appear as tilted, overlapping ellipses with different
  centres: the "slinky" look. The stream climbs.

#### 5.3 Rings (count, spacing, thickness, colour)

| | Reference | Live |
|---|---|---|
| Count | ≈10 full rings to the VP, plus the near frame ring at the bottom corners (0–160 × 1200–1536, 690–864 × 1220–1536) and the bottom arc (130–760 × 1440–1536) | ≈8–10 ring arcs, but they overlap and do not share a centre; no near frame ring at the bottom |
| Spacing (screen, ring tops on the VP column) | ≈105 → 60 → 25 → 20 → ≤15 px: smooth perspective falloff of evenly spaced rings | Irregular (e.g. 224, 273, 297, 370 on x=471); rings cross each other |
| Thickness / profile | **Flat band**, 26 px at the top of the outer ring (x=498, y 196–221), with a **double contour** (thin bright lip plus thick band) | **Round torus pipe** 17–22 px, often a pair of parallel thin pipes |
| Highlights | Evenly spaced bright "marquee" spots (≈12–16 per visible half-ring) and pale-yellow hot spots (#FCE082) | Smooth continuous specular streak; no marquee spots |
| Colour | Median **#F99649** (warm gold-copper); gold class 8% of frame | Median **#FF9F2F**, a yellower and more saturated orange; gold class **21%** of frame |

#### 5.4 Wall colour and perforation pattern

| | Reference | Live |
|---|---|---|
| Base colour | Magenta-violet metal: violet #992FC2, magenta #CD32AA; non-gold medians left wall #B830AE, right #D234AB, ceiling #B131A9 | Left lilac #BD5FD7, ceiling #C976FF, right wall **sky-blue #86C8FF** (41% of the right-wall box against 0.4% in the ref) |
| Specular | Strong white-pink streaks running along the tube length on every panel | Soft gradients; one overexposed white band across the middle (y≈500–700) |
| Perforations | **Capsule slots laid along the circumference**: horizontal dashes on the ceiling, vertical on the side walls, 3–5 rows per bay between rings, near slots ≈14×40 px, dark and high-contrast | Small dark-violet dashes (≈6×18 px) in long diagonal rows, lower contrast, no per-bay row structure |

#### 5.5 Nozzle lids

| | Reference | Live |
|---|---|---|
| Layout | Copper half-dome lids, one per bay, in a **symmetric row on each side wall** at ≈3 and 9 o'clock just above the waterline, shrinking toward the VP | One large flat red-orange disc in the top-right corner (≈610–864 × 0–300), at ceiling height |
| Positions (centres) | Left (140, 368) ≈150×105, (291, 444), (390, 468), (≈428, 480). Right (791, 462) ≈145×125, (663, 421), (599, 450), (569, 457) | n/a |

#### 5.6 Water: width, curves, colour bands

| | Reference | Live |
|---|---|---|
| Width | Fills the whole tube floor: ≈60 px at the VP → ≈420 px (49% of frame) at y=600 → full frame width from y≈800 | Narrow cyan channel in the mid-ground (≈110–120 px at y=900–1000) between pink bands and foam; reads as a ribbon, not a floor |
| Curves | The cyan core meanders: bottom centre → under Benny → (560, 700) → (450, 600) → (520, 520) → VP. ≈2 meanders, ±60–120 px | Bands run radially, straight up the rising tube; no S-meander |
| Colour | Cyan dominant: class 28% of frame, **#029AF3**. Two principal hot-pink S-bands **#F739E5** in the mid-ground. Rows y=1200/1400: **0% pink**, 83%/55% cyan | Cyan **#3993E7** (lighter, less saturated), 13% of frame. Pink dominates near the camera: row y=1200 41% pink / 12% cyan; row y=1400 51% pink / 26% cyan |
| Surface detail | White **4-point star glints**, glossy flow streaks | White motion streaks; no star glints |

#### 5.7 Foam, bubbles, splash

| | Reference | Live |
|---|---|---|
| Foam | **Cloud banks** of white-lavender clumps (#FCF6FF, 10–40 px puffs, soft lavender shading) hugging both edges from y≈540 to y≈1300 | Uniform white-pink spheres (≈30–60 px, #FFF0FF) strung along both banks (y≈730–1150) |
| Splash | A **V-shaped spray fan** of white/cyan droplets from Benny's base (180–680 × 1080–1260) | No spray fan; white streak particles near the bottom edge |
| Bubbles | ≈18 large iridescent bubbles (25–65 px) **at the sides** and ≈25 small; none over the path or Benny | Dozens of tiny 5–15 px bubbles across the whole frame, **including over Benny's hat**; ≈6 large bubbles drawn as faint thin outlines in the upper tube |

#### 5.8 Coins

| | Reference | Live |
|---|---|---|
| Count / line | ≈9–10, **centred on the stream ahead of Benny**, winding with the cyan core | ≈14 in a line to Benny's **left**, climbing to (≈380, 480) |
| Nearest coin | (473, 728), ≈95 px, ≈40 px above the pom-pom | (290, 1085), ≈135 px, overlapping the left edge of the hat |
| Orientation | Tilted to face the camera; rim thickness visible | Upright, mostly side-on to the camera |
| Colour / glyph | #F4B70F yellow-gold; embossed "$" legible | #FFBF33 orange-gold; the glyph does not read as "$" |

#### 5.9 Benny (proportions, position)

| | Reference | Live |
|---|---|---|
| Size / position | 27% of height, centre 49%, bottom 77% | 25%, centre 51%, bottom 94% |
| Hat : body | Hat including pom ≈62% of visible height; fur body below the cuff ≈38%; arm nubs at y≈1000–1080 | Hat dome ≈75%; fur only a fringe round the cuff (y≈1310–1450); no arm nubs visible |
| Hat | White and purple knit stripes (3 purple) with visible stitches and a purple ribbed cuff (#7513ED); pom-pom ≈140 px (#7F14EC) | Two wide smooth white stripes; ribbing only on the cuff; pom-pom ≈110 px and spikier (#AA4BFF) |
| Star | Yellow #F7BB19, **front-right of the cuff, facing the camera** (480–555 × 915–985) | Orange #FF9B1C, **edge-on on the right side** (535–590 × 1280–1360) |
| Fur | #F64EB1 | #FF55CB (lighter, more magenta) |

#### 5.10 HUD
Values are correct: `5/5`, `$ 1,420`, `05 · FLOW INTO THE CURRENT`, pause. Differences: the coin icon is ≈57 px at x 443–500
against ≈82 px at x 378–460; the value sits at x 537–638 against 495–620; the heart is smaller; the pill sits ≈6 px lower; the banner font is a narrower italic.

#### 5.11 Prioritised fix list for 05 (with acceptance checks)

| P | Owner | Task | Acceptance (re-capture at the same checkpoint) |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | PCT (+WEM) | Make the 05 checkpoint stretch a **straight, level tube** for ≥10 ring spacings ahead of the camera. Put the S-meander into the **water bands and lateral offset on the floor**, not the tube centreline. | Ring arcs concentric about a single point within ±10 px; that point at (498±25, 479±25) |
| P1 | PCT | Lower the camera's elevation over Benny and re-pitch so the VP stays at ≈31% y | Benny bbox ≈ x 230–612 / y 768–1190 (±25 px); full back, both arm nubs and the cuff star visible |
| P1 | WEM | Rings: flat gold bands (≈26 px at the outer ring top) with a double lip, marquee highlights and colour toward #F99649; remove the paired thin pipes | Gold class ≈6–12% of frame (ref 8%); no overlapping ring arcs |
| P1 | WEM | Walls: magenta-violet metal (#992FC2 / #CD32AA) with lengthwise white specular streaks; circumferential capsule slots, 3–5 rows per bay; **no sky-blue panels**; remove the mid-frame white glare | Pale-blue share in the right-wall box <2%; blow-out ≤ ref (3.9%) |
| P2 | WEM | Add 4 copper half-dome nozzle lids per side wall at the listed centres, one per bay | 8 lids visible, symmetric, shrinking toward the VP |
| P2 | WFX | Water fills the tube floor (≈49% of width at y=600, full width from y≈800). Cyan core #029AF3 dominant with 2 hot-pink S-bands (#F739E5) in the mid-ground, no pink in the near-centre, star glints | Cyan class ≈20–30% of frame; rows y=1200/1400 cyan-dominant |
| P2 | FBP | Cloud-like foam banks on both edges; a V-spray fan at Benny; ≈15–20 large iridescent bubbles at the sides; keep the centre path and Benny clear; cut the tiny-bubble count | No bubbles overlapping Benny's bbox; large bubbles clearly iridescent |
| P3 | AGE | Coins: ≈9–10 centred on the meander ahead of Benny, the first ≈40 px above the pom-pom at ≈95 px, tilted to face the camera; fix the "$" glyph; colour toward #F4B70F | No coin overlapping Benny; glyph reads "$" in the capture |
| P3 | BCA | Hat stripe pattern and knit texture as in the ref; star yellow and on the front-right of the cuff facing rear-camera views; ride waterline showing ≈38% body below the cuff | Star visible facing the camera in the 05 capture |
| P3 | AGE | HUD coin icon ≈82 px at x≈378–460; value at x≈495–620; heart ≈80 px | Pixel positions within ±10 px |
| P4 | PVQ | Re-capture 05, regenerate the side-by-side, overlay and diff; add the VP, Benny-bbox and ring-concentricity checks above to the report; refresh this section | New `qa/05_*` plus an updated section here |
| P4 | ABP | Re-measure triangles and draw calls after the lids, foam and bubbles go in (05 at `81e639e`: 625,575 triangles, 73 calls, SwiftShader) | Numbers logged; device fps if a device is available |

### 06 · CREST THE RINSE ARCH (interactive)

Verdict: the defining **arch** is not in frame. The camera is too close, and the walls and holes are the wrong pattern.

# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

entries.description:
Use this tool to list all tasks in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

- To see what tasks are available to work on (status: 'pending', no owner, not blocked)
- To check overall progress on the project
- To find tasks that are blocked and need dependencies resolved
- After completing a task, to check for newly unblocked work or claim the next available task
- **Prefer working on tasks in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple tasks are available, as earlier tasks often set up context for later ones

## Output

Returns a summary of each task:
- **id**: Task identifier (use with TaskGet, TaskUpdate)
- **subject**: Brief description of the task
- **status**: 'pending', 'in_progress', or 'completed'
- **owner**: Agent ID if assigned, empty if available
- **blockedBy**: List of open task IDs that must be resolved first (tasks with blockedBy cannot be claimed until dependencies resolve)

Use TaskGet with a specific task ID to view full details including description and comments.
entries.name: TaskList

entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

import sys
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
# usage: triptych.py out.png h label1=path1 label2=path2 ...
out, H = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2])
items = [a.split('=',1) for a in sys.argv[3:]]
ims = []
for lab, p in items:
    im = Image.open(p).convert('RGB')
    w = round(im.width * H / im.height)
    ims.append((lab, im.resize((w, H), Image.LANCZOS)))
pad, top = 8, 34
W = sum(i.width for _, i in ims) + pad * (len(ims) + 1)
canvas = Image.new('RGB', (W, H + top + pad), (24, 18, 32))
d = ImageDraw.Draw(canvas)
try: f = ImageFont.truetype('/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf', 20)

# Google Flow opening / ending videos

The game can play the user's Google Flow videos as silent cinematics and hand over to the real-time 3D
game without a cut. Gameplay (03–10) is always real-time 3D; the videos only cover the cinematics.

## Where to put the files

| File | Plays | Hand-off |
|---|---|---|
| `public/video/intro.mp4` (or `.webm`) | at launch and on Replay, instead of the real-time 01 | the live 3D intro is held at the "girl walks away" moment (`T.cp01`) under the video, then revealed by a 0.7 s cross-fade and continued in real time: 02 Whirlpool Tumble → 03 ride |
| `public/video/ending.mp4` (or `.webm`) — optional | when Benny reaches 11, before the victory frame | the real-time 11 frame (the official cartoon girl holds the towel, Benny hidden, **FINAL SPIN COMPLETE**) is revealed by a cross-fade |

If a file is missing, the real-time 3D cinematic plays instead. Videos are always muted and inline.
Tap skips the video (after 0.6 s).

## Recommended export

* Portrait 9:16 (1080×1920 or 720×1280) is best. Any ratio works edge to edge with no black bars and no stretching
  (`chooseVideoFit` in `src/ui/cinematicVideo.ts`):
  * **cover**: the clip is cropped to the phone when at least 78% of it stays visible. A 9:16 clip keeps 80% of its
    width on a 20:9 phone, so keep the girl, the towel and the washer door inside the centre ~80% of the frame.
    `?videoFocus=50% 40%` (CSS object-position) moves the crop centre for testing.
  * **fill**: if cropping would lose more (a 16:9 landscape Flow export, or a 9:16 clip on a 21:9 phone), the whole
    clip is shown over a soft blurred fill made from the same video frames instead of black bars.
* H.264 MP4 (AAC track optional — it is muted anyway). Keep it short (≈5–10 s) and under ~15 MB:
  the file is bundled into the Android APK.
* End the intro on the girl walking away from the closed washer door, seen from inside the drum if
  possible, so the cross-fade lands on the matching 3D shot. End the ending video just before the
  "girl holds the towel" pose.
* `.mp4` files are stored with Git LFS (see `.gitattributes`); the autosave backs them up automatically.

## Status (2026-11-15, account 3)

No Flow video is in the repository yet: `public/video/` holds only a placeholder note, so the game plays the
real-time 3D 01 opening. When the MP4 is ready, upload it and Claude will copy it to `public/video/intro.mp4`,
run `npm run test:cinematic`, rebuild the APK and push. No code change is needed.

## Testing

* Try a clip without copying it: `?introVideo=/path/under/project/root.mp4` (same for `endingVideo`);
  `?video=0` disables videos; QA captures (`?qa`) never play them.
* `npm run test:cinematic` — headless Chromium test of both paths (with a generated VP8 test clip and
  without any video). Result: `qa/cinematic_test.json`. Last run 2026-11-15: **pass** (overlay shown,
  3D held paused underneath, resumed after the fade and advanced 01 → 02; fallback without video OK).
  The test also checks edge-to-edge fit on a 20:9 phone (portrait clip → cover, landscape clip → blurred fill,
  no flat bar rows); screenshots in `qa/aspect/flow_video_*.png`.
  Note: this Chromium build has no H.264, so the automated test uses WebM; MP4 playback must be
  checked on a real Android device.

Implementation: `src/ui/cinematicVideo.ts`, hooks in `src/game/Game.ts` (`playIntroVideo`, `startOutro`).

WORLD LABS ATLAS / MARBLE + BLENDER + SPECIALISTS

I have compared the latest real 3D screenshot with my original approved "05 · FLOW INTO THE CURRENT" reference.

Continue in my existing Rainbow GitHub repository:

"josiahscalia5-dev/rainbow-"

Keep the original and recovery branches protected.

Preserve all eleven connected gameplay stages, Benny, my cartoon girl, the Google Flow video integration, and all existing functionality.

Maintain the five-minute GitHub backup while the development environment is active.

Open the approved Screen 05 reference and the latest actual game screenshot at full resolution.

Match the reference's:

Tunnel architecture: Deep metallic magenta-violet cylindrical drum, regular dark perforations, evenly spaced circular polished gold rings, small gold machinery fittings along the walls, and a deep illuminated tunnel extending into the distance.

Water: One broad, thick electric-cyan river with hot-pink swirling sections, strongly curved S-bends, glossy white-blue reflections, beautiful foam, and many transparent iridescent bubbles.

Lighting: Strong contrast, reflective gold, deep purple walls, luminous blue water, subtle bloom, and a warm golden glow far down the tunnel.

My World Labs connector is supposed to be connected to Claude.

Use the existing authenticated Atlas MCP tools.

Run "list_projects" first. Confirm whether the account has an active Atlas project and identify the tools available.

- "splats2Mesh" to obtain editable geometry.

Do not run paid generation tasks until I approve a specific estimated cost.

Create a working copy of my approved reference image.

Keep the original untouched.

Make a separate environment-only reference by removing or masking Benny, the HUD, coins, and other foreground game elements.

Preserve the tunnel geometry, wall pattern, gold rings, water route, depth, and lighting as reference information.

Use the cleaned reference and existing measured 3D tunnel geometry to guide reconstruction.

Avoid inventing a different level when generating unseen areas.

Import a Marble or Atlas export when available.

Align it with the existing Screen 05 course.

Measure tunnel diameter, ring spacing, water-channel width, camera position, and the path centerline.

Correct any incorrect geometry using Blender 5.3 and Python.

Save the refined Blender source and export suitable optimized assets for our Three.js Android game.

The World Labs output should accelerate modeling, not replace the playable scene with static imagery.

Coordinate the saved specialists without giving them conflicting file ownership.

The Environment Modeler fixes the tunnel and gold rings.

The Water FX Specialist rebuilds the moving cyan-and-pink current, wave shapes, reflections, and flowing surface.

The Foam and Bubble Specialist corrects the foam density, small bubbles, splashes, and iridescence.

The Camera Engineer matches the approved camera and tunnel depth.

The Benny Character Artist corrects Benny's proportions and white splash artifact.

The Reference Match Director checks the original image.

The Playwright Visual QA Specialist tests the real running game.

Use the other saved specialists wherever necessary.

Do not recreate my agents from scratch.

First fix the tunnel geometry and camera.

Then correct the gold-ring materials and wall colors.

Next fix the shape, movement, thickness, and colors of the water.

Then correct Benny, foam, bubbles, coins, and detailed lighting.

Use Playwright to render a new actual 3D game screenshot after each major correction.

Match the same camera and gameplay moment for comparison.

Do not use generated concept pictures as proof of actual gameplay.

8. GIVE ME VISUAL PROOF

Show the approved Screen 05 image and the updated actual game render side by side.

Also provide a transparent overlay comparison.

Check the geometry, perspective, colors, water shape, Benny proportions, and collectible positions.

Tell me which visual differences remain.

Do not claim 90–95% fidelity unless the actual screenshots support it.

Verify that the game is still playable, Screen 05 connects to Screen 06, and the existing Screen 07-to-08 deep descent is not broken.

9. PROTECT AND SAVE EVERYTHING

Commit the corrected scene, Blender source, World Labs assets (if generated), water shaders, specialist work, Playwright screenshots, QA reports, and updated progress notes.

Push to the verified current GitHub working branch.

Do not change the original approved images.

Do not spend external paid service credits without my approval.

START NOW: Verify World Labs access, complete the free preparation and comparison steps, and continue fixing my real 3D Screen 05 using the available tools.

I want my actual mobile game to look as close as possible to the approved artwork, not simply look colorful.

# Screen 05 — World Labs Atlas pilot plan (NOT RUN — awaiting approval)

Status 2026-11-15: the claude.ai **World Labs Atlas** connector is attached to the Rainbow session and its
10 tools load, but `list_projects` answers "this sign-in has no active Atlas account". Nothing has been
submitted and **no credits have been spent**. Every step below that uses credits needs the user's
explicit approval with the cost shown first.

## Inputs (prepared, originals untouched)

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `references/05_flow_into_the_current.png` | approved original, 864×1536, SHA-256 `d3f339d4…` (verified unchanged) |
| `qa/worldlabs/05/05_env_mask.png` | 8-bit mask on the same grid: 255 = keep (tunnel, rings, lids, water, foam, bubbles), 0 = exclude (HUD bar + stage label, Benny + splash, coin trail). 67 % of pixels kept |
| `qa/worldlabs/05/05_env_only_preview.png` | review image: the original with excluded areas greyed |

## Goal and honest expectations

Atlas reconstructs a scene from images as **posed RGBD views → Gaussian splats → optional GLB mesh**.
For Rainbow its value is **measurement and reference**, not finished game geometry:
* recover the reference camera (FOV, height, pitch) and a depth map of the tunnel, so the procedural
  tube radius, ring spacing/thickness, lid positions and water width can be calibrated to the image;
* optionally a splat/mesh of the tunnel section to load in Blender as a modelling underlay.
The playable tube, rings and animated cyan/pink water stay real-time Three.js geometry/shaders owned
by the environment modeler and the Water FX specialist (CLAUDE.md: no static splat/video substitutes).
A single stylised painting has no real parallax, so new views beyond ±10–15° are invented by the model
and must be checked against the reference before use.

## Proposed steps (cheapest, most useful first)

| # | Atlas tool | Purpose | Credits (official docs) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `list_projects` | confirm account, project, allowed tools, paid-work flag | free |
| 1 | `create_image_upload` + PUT | upload the approved 05 image (and mask) to the project | free (asset upload does not consume credits) |
| 2 | `images2PosedRGBD` (1 frame) | camera intrinsics/pose + per-pixel depth of the reference → measure tunnel radius, ring spacing, vanishing point, camera FOV | **not published** — read the rate card under Settings → Developer Platform before approving |
| 3 | `atlasChisel` (optional) | inpaint the masked areas (Benny/HUD/coins) to get a clean environment-only plate | **not published** (rate card) |
| 4 | `atlasGenerate` 8–12 views along the tube axis | extra consistent views down the tunnel for reconstruction | **not published** (rate card) |
| 5a | `posedImages2Splats` draft (`refine:false`) | quick splat check, ~30 s | **500 credits = $0.50** |
| 5b | `posedImages2Splats` refined | final splats, ~15–21 min | **5,000 credits = $5.00** |
| 6 | `splats2Mesh` | GLB mesh of the tunnel for Blender underlay | **not published** (rate card) |

Atlas billing: 1,000 credits = US$1; credits do not expire; a monthly spend limit can be set per account
or project (Settings → Developer Platform). Source: docs.atlas.worldlabs.ai/billing.md and
docs.atlas.worldlabs.ai/posed-images-to-splats.md (read 2026-11-15).

**Recommendation:** approve step 2 alone first (one call). Its depth/camera output is enough to calibrate
the manual build. Decide on 3–6 only after comparing that result with the reference.

## After Atlas (no extra credits)

1. Blender 5.3 (headless, installed): import depth/camera (and splats/mesh if made), measure ring spacing,
   tube radius, lid angles; write the numbers into the environment/course parameters.
2. Re-capture 05 with Playwright at 864×1536, compare against the reference and the manual-only build
   (`qa/pilot05/*`), and record time spent and corrections needed for A (Atlas-assisted) vs B (manual).
3. Keep the 07→08 61-unit descent and `npm run test:continuity` green.
- foam-bubbles-particles → water-fx-specialist (FYI, no action needed): since 19:30 `water.wake()` receives Benny's LIFTED body centre (Game.ts) and feeds `uBennyR` = the true waterline chord sqrt(0.86² − h²) ≈ 0.44 at the default 0.3 ride lift (it was 0.67, derived from the unlifted root, which made the contact band ~2× too wide). The bottom-of-frame white haze + blue dot field in 05/03 was the old `wakeV`/`tendrils` × `lace` term; your in-progress rewrite (no lace in wakeV) removes it. Splash fan / crown / spray / foam stay in riderSplash.ts, spray.ts, foam.ts as your comment says.
- foam-bubbles-particles → water-fx-specialist (wave 3, correction 7, ACTION NEEDED): the white elliptical band under Benny's fur (05, y≈1150–1170) is the `contact` term in `src/vfx/waterRibbon.ts` FRAG, Benny block (`if (rr < rb * 0.25) { … contact = … }` + `col = mix(col, uFoam * 1.2, clamp(contact * k, 0.0, 1.0));`). Evidence: `qa/pilot05/wave3/foam/iso0/05_noRibbonWake.png` (band gone) vs `05_noCrownSpray.png` (band stays with crown+spray hidden). Please delete that white mix entirely (the fur already hides the waterline; the ref has clear glossy cyan right under him). If you want a hint of contact, use at most `col += uCyanBright * 0.18 * (1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, rb * 0.3, rr)) * k;` (cyan, never uFoam/white). Keep the pink-band parting, `rings` and `wakeV` as they are. The V spray fan itself is mine (riderSplash.ts / spray.ts) and is being rebuilt as soft translucent white/cyan droplet streaks.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Environment-only clean plate of an approved Rainbow reference (for Marble / Atlas input).

The original reference is only READ, never written. Output goes to a separate folder.

    python3 -I tools/make_env_plate.py references/05_flow_into_the_current.png \
        qa/worldlabs/05/05_env_mask.png qa/worldlabs/05 --vp 498,479

mask: 255 = keep (real reference pixels), 0 = remove (HUD, Benny + splash, coins).
Fill strategy (everything filled is INVENTED and marked in *_fill_mask.png):
  * wall / ceiling holes (above the vanishing point): rotate the reference about the VP. The tunnel is
    close to rotationally symmetric there, so rings stay rings and slots stay circumferential.
  * floor holes (below the VP): sample outward along the ray from the VP to the first real pixel
    (near the camera the water bands run roughly radially, so this continues them).
  * a narrow seam is blended with OpenCV Telea inpainting.
"""
import argparse
import math
from pathlib import Path

import cv2
import numpy as np


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("ref")
    ap.add_argument("mask")
    ap.add_argument("outdir")
    ap.add_argument("--vp", default="498,479")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    ref = cv2.imread(a.ref, cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)
    keep = cv2.imread(a.mask, cv2.IMREAD_GRAYSCALE) > 127
    h, w = keep.shape
    vx, vy = (float(v) for v in a.vp.split(","))
    out = ref.copy()
    filled = np.zeros((h, w), bool)
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:h, 0:w].astype(np.float32)
    dx, dy = xx - vx, yy - vy
    hole = ~keep

    # 1. walls/ceiling: rotation about the VP (try growing angles both ways)
    upper = hole & (yy < vy - 8)
    for deg in (22, -22, 30, -30, 38, -38, 46, -46, 55, -55, 65, -65):
        todo = upper & ~filled
        if not todo.any():
            break
        t = math.radians(deg)
        sx = vx + dx * math.cos(t) - dy * math.sin(t)
        sy = vy + dx * math.sin(t) + dy * math.cos(t)
        ix, iy = np.round(sx).astype(int), np.round(sy).astype(int)
        inb = (ix >= 0) & (ix < w) & (iy >= 0) & (iy < h)
        ok = todo & inb
        ok[ok] = keep[iy[ok], ix[ok]] & (iy[ok] < vy - 8)
        out[ok] = ref[iy[ok], ix[ok]]
        filled |= ok

    # 2. floor (and anything left): first real pixel outward along the VP ray
    rest = hole & ~filled
    ys, xs = np.nonzero(rest)
    for s in np.linspace(1.02, 6.0, 250):
        if len(ys) == 0:
            break
        sx = np.round(vx + (xs - vx) * s).astype(int)
        sy = np.round(vy + (ys - vy) * s).astype(int)
        inb = (sx >= 0) & (sx < w) & (sy >= 0) & (sy < h)
        ok = np.zeros(len(ys), bool)
        ok[inb] = keep[sy[inb], sx[inb]]
        out[ys[ok], xs[ok]] = ref[sy[ok], sx[ok]]
        filled[ys[ok], xs[ok]] = True
        ys, xs = ys[~ok], xs[~ok]

    # 3. whatever is still empty + a seam around every fill region: Telea inpainting
    seam = cv2.dilate(hole.astype(np.uint8), np.ones((7, 7), np.uint8)) & cv2.erode(
        (~hole).astype(np.uint8) * 0 + hole.astype(np.uint8), np.ones((1, 1), np.uint8))
    border = cv2.dilate(hole.astype(np.uint8), np.ones((5, 5), np.uint8)) - cv2.erode(hole.astype(np.uint8), np.ones((5, 5), np.uint8))
    left = (hole & ~filled).astype(np.uint8)
    out = cv2.inpaint(out, np.clip(border + left, 0, 1).astype(np.uint8) * 255, 4, cv2.INPAINT_TELEA)
    del seam

    od = Path(a.outdir)
    od.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    stem = Path(a.ref).stem.split("_")[0]
    cv2.imwrite(str(od / f"{stem}_env_clean_plate.png"), out)
    cv2.imwrite(str(od / f"{stem}_env_fill_mask.png"), (hole * 255).astype(np.uint8))
    # review sheet: original | clean plate | invented pixels tinted
    tint = out.copy()
    tint[hole] = (0.55 * tint[hole] + 0.45 * np.array([60, 220, 60])).astype(np.uint8)
    sheet = np.concatenate([ref, np.full((h, 8, 3), 30, np.uint8), out, np.full((h, 8, 3), 30, np.uint8), tint], 1)
    cv2.imwrite(str(od / f"{stem}_env_plate_review.png"), sheet)
    print("invented share:", round(float(hole.mean()), 4), "rotation-filled:", round(float((filled & (yy < vy)).mean()), 4))


if __name__ == "__main__":

"""Environment-only clean plate of an approved Rainbow reference (for Marble / Atlas input).

The original reference is only READ, never written. Output goes to a separate folder.

    python3 -I tools/make_env_plate.py references/05_flow_into_the_current.png \
        qa/worldlabs/05/05_env_mask.png qa/worldlabs/05 --vp 498,479

mask: 255 = keep (real reference pixels), 0 = remove (HUD, Benny + splash, coins).
Fill strategy (everything filled is INVENTED and marked in *_fill_mask.png):
  * wall / ceiling holes (above the vanishing point): rotate the reference about the VP. The tunnel is
    close to rotationally symmetric there, so rings stay rings and slots stay circumferential.
  * floor holes (below the VP): sample outward along the ray from the VP to the first real pixel
    (near the camera the water bands run roughly radially, so this continues them).
  * a narrow seam is blended with OpenCV Telea inpainting.
"""
import argparse
import math
from pathlib import Path

import cv2
import numpy as np


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("ref")
    ap.add_argument("mask")
    ap.add_argument("outdir")
    ap.add_argument("--vp", default="498,479")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    ref = cv2.imread(a.ref, cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)
    keep = cv2.imread(a.mask, cv2.IMREAD_GRAYSCALE) > 127
    h, w = keep.shape
    vx, vy = (float(v) for v in a.vp.split(","))
    out = ref.copy()
    filled = np.zeros((h, w), bool)
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:h, 0:w].astype(np.float32)
    dx, dy = xx - vx, yy - vy
    hole = ~keep

    # 1. walls/ceiling: rotation about the VP (try growing angles both ways)
    upper = hole & (yy < vy - 8)
    for deg in (22, -22, 30, -30, 38, -38, 46, -46, 55, -55, 65, -65):
        todo = upper & ~filled
        if not todo.any():
            break
        t = math.radians(deg)
        sx = vx + dx * math.cos(t) - dy * math.sin(t)
        sy = vy + dx * math.sin(t) + dy * math.cos(t)
        ix, iy = np.round(sx).astype(int), np.round(sy).astype(int)
        inb = (ix >= 0) & (ix < w) & (iy >= 0) & (iy < h)
        ok = todo & inb
        ok[ok] = keep[iy[ok], ix[ok]] & (iy[ok] < vy - 8)
        out[ok] = ref[iy[ok], ix[ok]]
        filled |= ok

    # 2. floor (and anything left): first real pixel outward along the VP ray
    rest = hole & ~filled
    ys, xs = np.nonzero(rest)
    for s in np.linspace(1.02, 6.0, 250):
        if len(ys) == 0:
            break
        sx = np.round(vx + (xs - vx) * s).astype(int)
        sy = np.round(vy + (ys - vy) * s).astype(int)
        inb = (sx >= 0) & (sx < w) & (sy >= 0) & (sy < h)
        ok = np.zeros(len(ys), bool)
        ok[inb] = keep[sy[inb], sx[inb]]
        out[ys[ok], xs[ok]] = ref[sy[ok], sx[ok]]
        filled[ys[ok], xs[ok]] = True
        ys, xs = ys[~ok], xs[~ok]

    # 3. whatever is still empty + a seam around every fill region: Telea inpainting
    seam = cv2.dilate(hole.astype(np.uint8), np.ones((7, 7), np.uint8)) & cv2.erode(
        (~hole).astype(np.uint8) * 0 + hole.astype(np.uint8), np.ones((1, 1), np.uint8))
    border = cv2.dilate(hole.astype(np.uint8), np.ones((5, 5), np.uint8)) - cv2.erode(hole.astype(np.uint8), np.ones((5, 5), np.uint8))
    left = (hole & ~filled).astype(np.uint8)
    out = cv2.inpaint(out, np.clip(border + left, 0, 1).astype(np.uint8) * 255, 4, cv2.INPAINT_TELEA)
    del seam

    od = Path(a.outdir)
    od.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    stem = Path(a.ref).stem.split("_")[0]
    cv2.imwrite(str(od / f"{stem}_env_clean_plate.png"), out)
    cv2.imwrite(str(od / f"{stem}_env_fill_mask.png"), (hole * 255).astype(np.uint8))
    # review sheet: original | clean plate | invented pixels tinted
    tint = out.copy()
    tint[hole] = (0.55 * tint[hole] + 0.45 * np.array([60, 220, 60])).astype(np.uint8)
    sheet = np.concatenate([ref, np.full((h, 8, 3), 30, np.uint8), out, np.full((h, 8, 3), 30, np.uint8), tint], 1)
    cv2.imwrite(str(od / f"{stem}_env_plate_review.png"), sheet)
    print("invented share:", round(float(hole.mean()), 4), "rotation-filled:", round(float((filled & (yy < vy)).mean()), 4))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import argparse
import math
from pathlib import Path

import cv2
import numpy as np


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("ref")
    ap.add_argument("mask")
    ap.add_argument("outdir")
    ap.add_argument("--vp", default="498,479")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    ref = cv2.imread(a.ref, cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)
    keep = cv2.imread(a.mask, cv2.IMREAD_GRAYSCALE) > 127
    h, w = keep.shape
    vx, vy = (float(v) for v in a.vp.split(","))
    out = ref.copy()
    filled = np.zeros((h, w), bool)
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:h, 0:w].astype(np.float32)
    dx, dy = xx - vx, yy - vy
    hole = ~keep

    # 1. walls/ceiling: rotation about the VP (try growing angles both ways)
    upper = hole & (yy < vy - 8)
    for deg in (22, -22, 30, -30, 38, -38, 46, -46, 55, -55, 65, -65):
        todo = upper & ~filled
        if not todo.any():
            break
        t = math.radians(deg)
        sx = vx + dx * math.cos(t) - dy * math.sin(t)
        sy = vy + dx * math.sin(t) + dy * math.cos(t)
        ix, iy = np.round(sx).astype(int), np.round(sy).astype(int)
        inb = (ix >= 0) & (ix < w) & (iy >= 0) & (iy < h)
        ok = todo & inb
        ok[ok] = keep[iy[ok], ix[ok]] & (iy[ok] < vy - 8)
        out[ok] = ref[iy[ok], ix[ok]]
        filled |= ok

    # 2. floor (and anything left): first real pixel outward along the VP ray
    rest = hole & ~filled
    ys, xs = np.nonzero(rest)
    for s in np.linspace(1.02, 6.0, 250):
        if len(ys) == 0:
            break
        sx = np.round(vx + (xs - vx) * s).astype(int)
        sy = np.round(vy + (ys - vy) * s).astype(int)
        inb = (sx >= 0) & (sx < w) & (sy >= 0) & (sy < h)
        ok = np.zeros(len(ys), bool)
        ok[inb] = keep[sy[inb], sx[inb]]
        out[ys[ok], xs[ok]] = ref[sy[ok], sx[ok]]
        filled[ys[ok], xs[ok]] = True
        ys, xs = ys[~ok], xs[~ok]

    seam = cv2.dilate(hole.astype(np.uint8), np.ones((7, 7), np.uint8)) & cv2.erode(
        (~hole).astype(np.uint8) * 0 + hole.astype(np.uint8), np.ones((1, 1), np.uint8))
    border = cv2.dilate(hole.astype(np.uint8), np.ones((5, 5), np.uint8)) - cv2.erode(hole.astype(np.uint8), np.ones((5, 5), np.uint8))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Environment-only clean plate of an approved Rainbow reference (for Marble / Atlas input).

The original reference is only READ, never written. Output goes to a separate folder.

    python3 -I tools/make_env_plate.py references/05_flow_into_the_current.png \
        qa/worldlabs/05/05_env_mask.png qa/worldlabs/05 --vp 498,479

mask: 255 = keep (real reference pixels), 0 = remove (HUD, Benny + splash, coins).
Fill strategy (everything filled is INVENTED and marked in *_fill_mask.png):
  * wall / ceiling holes (above the vanishing point): rotate the reference about the VP. The tunnel is
    close to rotationally symmetric there, so rings stay rings and slots stay circumferential.
  * floor holes (below the VP): sample outward along the ray from the VP to the first real pixel
    (near the camera the water bands run roughly radially, so this continues them).
  * a narrow seam is blended with OpenCV Telea inpainting.
"""
import argparse
import math
from pathlib import Path

import cv2
import numpy as np


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("ref")
    ap.add_argument("mask")
    ap.add_argument("outdir")
    ap.add_argument("--vp", default="498,479")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    ref = cv2.imread(a.ref, cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)
    keep = cv2.imread(a.mask, cv2.IMREAD_GRAYSCALE) > 127
    h, w = keep.shape
    vx, vy = (float(v) for v in a.vp.split(","))
    out = ref.copy()
    filled = np.zeros((h, w), bool)
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:h, 0:w].astype(np.float32)
    dx, dy = xx - vx, yy - vy
    hole = ~keep

    def apply(region: np.ndarray, rot_deg: float, zoom: float, same_half: str) -> None:
        """copy real pixels through a similarity about the VP (rotation + zoom keeps texture unstreaked)"""
        nonlocal filled
        todo = region & ~filled
        if not todo.any():
            return
        t = math.radians(rot_deg)
        sx = vx + zoom * (dx * math.cos(t) - dy * math.sin(t))
        sy = vy + zoom * (dx * math.sin(t) + dy * math.cos(t))
        ix, iy = np.round(sx).astype(int), np.round(sy).astype(int)
        ok = todo & (ix >= 0) & (ix < w) & (iy >= 0) & (iy < h)
        ok[ok] = (keep if same_half == "upper" else water)[iy[ok], ix[ok]] & (
            (iy[ok] < vy - 8) if same_half == "upper" else (iy[ok] > vy + 8))
        out[ok] = ref[iy[ok], ix[ok]]
        filled |= ok

    # 1. walls/ceiling: rotation about the VP, then zoom toward it for the corners
    upper = hole & (yy < vy - 8)
    for deg in (22, -22, 30, -30, 38, -38, 46, -46, 55, -55, 65, -65):
        apply(upper, deg, 1.0, "upper")
    for z in (0.85, 0.75, 0.65, 0.55, 0.45):
        for deg in (0, 15, -15, 30, -30):
            apply(upper, deg, z, "upper")

    # 2. floor: water texture from the same half; rotation first (keeps the perspective scale),
    #    then zoom outward (nearer water) for the large area behind Benny
    lower = hole & ~upper
    for deg in (30, -30, 40, -40, 50, -50, 60, -60):
        apply(lower & (np.hypot(dx, dy) < 330), deg, 1.0, "lower")
    for z in (1.35, 1.6, 1.9, 2.3, 2.8, 3.4, 4.2, 5.2):
        for deg in (0, 12, -12, 25, -25):
            apply(lower, deg, z, "lower")

    h8 = hole.astype(np.uint8)
    border = cv2.dilate(h8, np.ones((5, 5), np.uint8)) - cv2.erode(h8, np.ones((5, 5), np.uint8))

    out = cv2.inpaint(out, np.clip(border + left, 0, 1).astype(np.uint8) * 255, 4, cv2.INPAINT_TELEA)

    cv2.imwrite(str(od / f"{stem}_env_fill_mask.png"), (hole * 255).astype(np.uint8))

    tint = out.copy()
    tint[hole] = (0.55 * tint[hole] + 0.45 * np.array([60, 220, 60])).astype(np.uint8)
    sheet = np.concatenate([ref, np.full((h, 8, 3), 30, np.uint8), out, np.full((h, 8, 3), 30, np.uint8), tint], 1)
    cv2.imwrite(str(od / f"{stem}_env_plate_review.png"), sheet)

# World Labs

Create with Atlas APIs and tools.

Agent skills for World Labs Atlas, packaged as one plugin for Codex and Claude Code.

| Skill | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `atlas-flythrough` | Make a camera-move video through a scene from one or more images. |
| `atlas-splats` | Turn one or more images into a 3D scene as Gaussian splats. |
| `atlas-blender` | See and shape Atlas scenes in Blender: posed images as cameras and point clouds, a camera path on the timeline, native splats. The Atlas add-on is optional. |
| `worldlabs-cli` | Set up the World Labs CLI and run any other Atlas API task with it. |

## How the skills are built

Edit the skills from these ideas. When a session shows a problem, find which idea the text
failed to carry and fix that, instead of appending a rule.

- **The person directs; the agent does the work.** Where the work happens and what the result
  should be are the person's decisions. Asking is the default for those: the agent asks each in
  one line, and decides for itself only when the person says outright not to ask. Once they are
  settled the agent carries the work through to the result. It shows each stage as it lands and
  does not quote prices or ask for a go-ahead before a step.
- **Blender is the preferred place** when it is installed, because both of them can see the
  scene in 3D. The Atlas add-on is optional.
- **Build the scene first, then make things from it.** The scene is explored outward in rounds
  of a few views, each placed from what the last revealed, until it is blocked out with no gaps
  (a room takes 12 to 16 views), before any video or reconstruction. Building the scene is a
  job on its own too: a request for new angles of an image is done the same way.
  The path or the splats come from the scene,
  and each result is looked at before it is handed over.
- **The skills are the method; the docs are reference.** A workflow skill and its scene file
  hold everything needed to do the work. Agents open the docs for a task's fields and limits,
  not for how to do the workflow.
- **Say what good looks like.** The skills describe a good path or a good set of views and leave
  the camera placement to the agent. Code appears only for calls to our own tools.
- **Hand over things the person can use:** the video or splats, the project file, and what the
  model invented.
- **Method and place are separate.** `atlas-flythrough` and `atlas-splats` hold the method.
  `atlas-blender` and `worldlabs-cli` hold how to do it in one place. Each skill is complete
  without the others, so the two method skills carry identical copies of their shared material;
  see [Development](#development).

## Install

### ChatGPT

Install World Labs from the ChatGPT plugin directory and connect your World Labs account. The hosted
connection runs the Atlas tasks: generating images and views, estimating cameras and depth,
reconstructing Gaussian splats, and extracting meshes. The plugin carries every skill in this
repository and its supporting files. The video, splats and CLI skills are written for a shell
with the World Labs CLI, and the Atlas for Blender skill requires a compatible local Blender
environment; a hosted chat without that access uses the connected tools. The plugin does not
install Blender, its extension, or the World Labs CLI.

### Codex

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add worldlabsai/skills
codex plugin add worldlabs@worldlabs
./plugin.json
---
name: worldlabs-cli
description: Run World Labs Atlas API tasks from a terminal with the worldlabs CLI. Covers install and sign-in, uploading files, running a task from a JSON request, waiting for it, and downloading its outputs. Use for any Atlas job without a skill of its own, such as generating or editing an image, estimating camera and depth, or extracting a mesh, and for CLI setup and errors. New views of a scene belong to atlas-splats or atlas-flythrough. Also covers the connected World Labs tools when there is no shell.
license: Apache-2.0
compatibility: Needs Node.js 22 or newer and network access to api.atlas.worldlabs.ai.
---

# World Labs CLI

`worldlabs` runs Atlas API tasks. Every task works the same way: upload the files it needs, write
its request as JSON, run it, wait, and download what it made.

For a video or camera move use the `atlas-flythrough` skill, for a 3D scene as splats use
`atlas-splats`, and for work inside Blender use `atlas-blender`. New views of a place from an
image (other angles, the far side, more of the room) are building a scene, which is the first
part of both workflows: use either of those skills for them, even when the person has not yet
chosen a video or splats. This skill covers setup and every other task.

## Set up

```sh
npm install -g @worldlabsai/cli@latest
worldlabs auth status
```

If the status check reports no key, have the person run `worldlabs auth login` in their own
terminal and enter the key at its private prompt. Never ask for a key in chat or put one in a
command. Automation can set `WLT_API_KEY`. The key selects the API project and its billing. A
passing status check confirms asset access, not every task's permission.

The CLI needs network access. In a sandbox that blocks it, ask for approval instead of retrying.

## Run a task

```sh
worldlabs tasks list                                        # task names
worldlabs assets upload photo.jpg --json                    # note the "id"
worldlabs tasks run <task> --request request.json --wait --json > op.json
worldlabs operations download <operation-id> --out results
```

"""
Import a World Labs export (Marble world GLB mesh / PLY splats, or an Atlas splats2Mesh GLB) into
Blender, align it to the Rainbow tube convention, measure it, and write a light underlay for the
environment modeler. It costs no World Labs credits: it only reads files you already exported.

    blender -b --python tools/blender/import_world_asset.py -- \
        --in path/to/world.glb [--ply path/to/splats.ply] \
        --name marble05 [--target-radius 7.6] [--decimate 0.25] [--out-dir qa/worldlabs/05/import]

Outputs (in --out-dir):
  <name>_underlay.glb    aligned, scaled, decimated mesh (tunnel axis = -Z, i.e. Three.js forward;
                         centre line on the origin; radius scaled to --target-radius)
  <name>.blend           the Blender scene (original import kept in its own hidden collection)
  <name>_measure.json    axis, length, radius stats, ring-like cross-section peaks, scale applied
  <name>_preview.png     Workbench render from the tunnel axis looking down -Z (rear-camera view)

The underlay is a modelling/measurement aid. The playable tube, rings and animated water stay
real-time Three.js geometry/shaders (CLAUDE.md: no static substitutes in gameplay).
"""
import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import sys

import bpy
import numpy as np
from mathutils import Matrix, Vector


def parse_args():
    argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:] if "--" in sys.argv else []
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--in", dest="inp", required=True, help="GLB/GLTF mesh exported from Marble or Atlas")
    ap.add_argument("--ply", default=None, help="optional PLY splats/points to import alongside (not aligned by PCA)")
    ap.add_argument("--name", default="world")
    ap.add_argument("--target-radius", type=float, default=7.6, help="Rainbow 05 tube radius (src/world/course.ts)")
    ap.add_argument("--decimate", type=float, default=0.25, help="collapse ratio for the underlay (1 = keep all)")
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", default="qa/worldlabs/import")
    ap.add_argument("--no-preview", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--flip", action="store_true", help="reverse the detected tunnel direction")
    return ap.parse_args(argv)


def reset_scene():

content.text:
Your new message is in hand, and the five specialists already running have been given your new work order and rejection list. Here is where things stand while they work.

**World Labs Atlas.** I ran `list_projects` first, as you asked. It fails with "this sign-in has no active Atlas account", so nothing was generated or spent.
- **What's missing:** the World Labs login used by the claude.ai connector has no Atlas account yet.
- **What you need to do:** open https://atlas.worldlabs.ai with that same login and finish signing up. Then add credits under Settings → Developer Platform, ideally with a spending limit.
- **After that:** tell me, and I'll re-run the free check and show you the price of each step before running anything.

**Marble.** It isn't connected here. The World Labs plugin and connector cover Atlas only and have no Marble tools, so you'd use Marble yourself in the browser. I prepared everything for that in `qa/worldlabs/05/MARBLE_MANUAL.md`:
- **What to upload:** `05_env_clean_plate_cropped.png`, a copy of your approved image with the HUD rows cropped off. Benny, the splash and the coin trail are filled with water copied from the reference itself. Your original is unchanged; I re-checked all 12 reference files.
- **What's invented:** the fill covers 33.7% of the frame, and `05_env_fill_mask.png` shows exactly which pixels. The river centre where Benny stood is a visible patchwork with a soft grey smear at its lower edge. A cleaner version would need a generative fill, either Atlas (paid) or an image editor you use yourself.
- **The prompt:** a ready-to-paste Marble prompt that describes only your tunnel and asks for no redesign.
- **The return trip:** export the `.glb`/`.ply` from Marble and give it to me. The saved Blender import tool will line it up with the Screen 05 course, measure it, and save a `.blend` file for the Environment Modeler.

**Specialists, in the order you set.** The Camera Engineer goes first and will publish a "camera lock". The others then make their final measurements against that locked view.
- **Environment Modeler:** has your list of rejected items (oversized orange loops, floating crossbars, pale pink walls), plus a request to save a Blender source of the corrected fittings.
- **Water FX Specialist:** has deleted the white band under Benny, which the Foam specialist traced to a white "contact" effect in the water shader.
- **Foam and Bubble Specialist:** is rebuilding the foam, bubbles and splash fan.
- **Benny Character Artist:** is making the hat smaller relative to a rounder body, and checking whether his fur adds any white fringe.

I also fixed a bug in the shared capture script. It was silently ignoring the settings for hiding individual effects, which the specialists use to test parts of the image in isolation.

When the five finish, the Reference Match Director and the Playwright Visual QA Specialist will produce the side-by-side and overlay comparisons from the real running game. After that I'll run the gameplay, 05→06 and 07→08 continuity, and Android tests, then push.
